summary: Quickstart Python RAG template times out when ingesting/querying larger documents (default timeouts + retrieval settings)
description:
Issue summary
Customer reports the Python Quickstart RAG template (FastAPI + ingestion worker) is timing out when ingesting or querying larger documents (multi-MB PDFs / long markdown exports). Small docs work.

Impact
- Blocks customer evaluation / onboarding path. Customer cannot complete demo with their real knowledge base.
- Symptoms: ingestion job appears to hang then fails; query endpoint returns 504 / client timeout.

Customer context
- Customer: Devkit AI (self-serve)
- Use case: internal product docs + runbooks (several 2–10MB docs, some with tables)
- Running: local Docker Compose for vector DB + template app; calling Redwood Hosted API for embeddings + chat

Environment
- Template: Python RAG quickstart (FastAPI)
- Region: us-east
- Model route: redwood/llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Vector backend: default template backend (Postgres + pgvector via docker-compose)
- Telemetry: OpenTelemetry enabled; customer provided request_id + trace_id from template logs

Steps to reproduce (confirmed internally)
1) Start the Python RAG template with default .env values.
2) Ingest a single large document (~6MB markdown or PDF extracted text ~500k–900k chars).
3) Run the query endpoint with a question that triggers retrieval.

Expected
- Ingestion completes (even if slower) or provides clear guidance on required config.
- Queries return within a reasonable bound, with bounded retrieval work.

Actual
- Ingestion frequently fails with client timeout after ~30s–60s or appears stuck.
- Query endpoint intermittently exceeds default request timeout; caller sees timeout / 504.

Observed logs (customer-provided excerpts)
- 2026-01-20T18:12:09Z level=INFO service=rag-api event=request.start request_id=rwreq_01HP8Q0TQ2T1C6 trace_id=3d2f6d5c1a5c9f0a4a7d9f1d9a3b1c2 tenant=devkitai route=/v1/rag/ingest doc_bytes=6428911
- 2026-01-20T18:12:39Z level=ERROR service=rag-api event=request.error request_id=rwreq_01HP8Q0TQ2T1C6 trace_id=3d2f6d5c1a5c9f0a4a7d9f1d9a3b1c2 error_class=timeout error_message="upstream request timed out" duration_ms=30041
- 2026-01-20T18:14:22Z level=ERROR service=rag-api event=request.error request_id=rwreq_01HP8Q4X6G6V6F trace_id=2c1d0d0b2f9d5a44c0df3e9c6c8a1a0 error_class=timeout error_message="RAG retrieval exceeded deadline" duration_ms=30002

Initial hypothesis
- Default template timeouts are too aggressive for large-doc ingestion (lots of embedding calls + slow pgvector insert/index churn).
- Query path allows too many chunks / too-large context, causing additional latency and pushing the request over defaults.

Investigation notes
- Reproduced with a 7MB markdown doc on a laptop + docker-compose pgvector.
- In default config, ingestion does embedding requests in relatively small batches and waits synchronously; total wall time can exceed 30s on larger docs.
- Query path had insufficient bounding defaults:
  - Retrieval could return too many chunks (high k) when the doc is large.
  - Chunk size/overlap defaults generate many chunks, amplifying embed/insert work.
- Not an outage in Hosted API; this is primarily template configuration + defaults for local dev.

Workaround / recommended config (sent to customer)
1) Increase request/client timeout for ingestion + query while keeping per-step deadlines:
   - RW_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S=120
   - RW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=120000
   - RAG_RETRIEVAL_TIMEOUT_MS=1500 (keep retrieval bounded)
2) Bound retrieval and context to avoid runaway latency:
   - RAG_TOP_K=6
   - RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1800
   - RAG_RERANK_TOP_N=20 (if reranking is enabled)
3) Reduce chunk explosion on large docs:
   - RAG_CHUNK_SIZE=900
   - RAG_CHUNK_OVERLAP=80
4) Increase ingestion batching/concurrency (safer defaults, still rate-limit friendly):
   - RAG_INGEST_EMBED_BATCH_SIZE=64
   - RAG_INGEST_CONCURRENCY=4
5) If running docker-compose locally, allocate more resources to the DB container and ensure indexes are created after bulk insert:
   - (Docker Desktop) Memory >= 6GB for stable ingest of multi-MB docs

Resolution
- Confirmed root cause is a mismatch between template defaults (timeouts + unbounded-ish retrieval settings) and larger-doc workloads.
- Provided customer with a config block and guidance.
- Opened a follow-up PR to adjust template defaults + improve docs and error messages so users get actionable next steps instead of a generic timeout.

Follow-up PR
- redwood-quickstarts#402: "Fix papercuts from dogfooding — env var naming consistency, clearer README, and improved error messages" (includes: updated default timeouts for ingestion route, bounded retrieval defaults, and README section for large-doc ingestion tuning)

Customer-visible next steps
- Customer to retry with updated config; if still failing, request a trace export (trace_id + span timings) and sample doc characteristics (bytes, extracted text length, number of chunks).

2026-01-20 18:32 UTC — Dev Patel (Reporter)
Customer (Devkit AI) says they can ingest small docs but large doc ingest fails around ~30s. They provided request_id rwreq_01HP8Q0TQ2T1C6 and trace_id 3d2f6d5c1a5c9f0a4a7d9f1d9a3b1c2. Asking DX to confirm whether this is expected with defaults.

2026-01-20 19:10 UTC — Owen Phillips (Support)
Pulled Console traces using trace_id. No abnormal API-side errors; looks like client/template-side timeout before ingest completes. Span breakdown shows long embed loop + DB insert time. Suggest bumping RW_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S and batching embeddings.

2026-01-21 00:05 UTC — Sabrina James (Assignee)
Repro’d locally with 6–7MB markdown. Default RW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (30s) is too low for ingest. Also RAG_TOP_K and chunking defaults produce too many chunks in larger docs, causing query timeouts. Drafting recommended env vars + README section for "large docs" tuning.

2026-01-21 00:22 UTC — Sabrina James
Sent customer workaround:
- RW_HTTP_TIMEOUT_S=120
- RW_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=120000
- RAG_TOP_K=6
- RAG_CHUNK_SIZE=900 / RAG_CHUNK_OVERLAP=80
- RAG_INGEST_EMBED_BATCH_SIZE=64
- RAG_INGEST_CONCURRENCY=4
Asked them to confirm if they’re behind a proxy/VPN and to share extracted text length if still slow.

2026-01-22 17:48 UTC — Dev Patel
Customer confirms ingest completes with longer timeout + batching, but query still occasionally times out with complex questions. They also noticed latency spikes when reranking is enabled. Requesting guidance for safe bounds.

2026-01-22 19:03 UTC — Sabrina James
Recommended bounding query work:
- RAG_RETRIEVAL_TIMEOUT_MS=1500
- RAG_RERANK_TOP_N=20
- RAG_MAX_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1800
Also suggested keeping RAG_TOP_K <= 8 for local pgvector. This keeps the demo predictable and aligns with template goals (production shape, bounded latency).

2026-01-23 02:16 UTC — Sean Gallagher (SRE)
+1 to bounding retrieval. Don’t increase timeouts without adding per-stage budgets; otherwise we get long-hanging requests and noisy retries. Suggest adding clearer error taxonomy in template: timeout.retrieval vs timeout.upstream vs timeout.db.

2026-01-24 21:40 UTC — Sabrina James
Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/402
Changes include: improved README guidance for large docs, more conservative/bounded retrieval defaults, and clearer timeout errors (with suggested env vars). Linking SDK timeout guidance as well.

2026-01-26 16:12 UTC — Dev Patel
Customer confirms success after applying bounds + updated defaults from PR branch. Closing ticket; keeping an eye on any follow-on 429/backoff confusion (see SUP-2949).
